title: "Confidence Interval for Population Mean Difference"
format: html

## Question 1 (4 points)

A team of chemists is studying whether a new catalyst reduces the time required for a particular chemical reaction (in seconds). To control for variability in materials, temperature, and equipment, each trial is performed twice using the same batch of chemicals - once without the catalyst and once with the catalyst. The batch is split into two equal portions to ensure the same material is tested both ways, and both portions are run under identical conditions (same temperature, pressure, etc.). They do this 40 times and take the difference between the two runs of the experiment and compute the mean and standard deviation of these differences (1.6 and 1.5 respectively).

In the code block below, construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean difference in reaction times. THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
xbar_d <- 1.6
s_d <- 1.5
n <- 40
alpha <- 0.05
t_quant <- qt(1-alpha/2, n-1)

xbar_d + c(-1, 1)*t_quant*s_d/sqrt(n)
```

[We are 95% confident that the true mean difference in reaction times is between 1.1203 and 2.0797 seconds.]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 2 (4 points)

Economists are interested in whether the average trade balance (exports minus imports, measured in billions of dollars) has changed for a set of countries after a major new trade agreement went into effect.

For each of 30 countries, they record the country’s trade balance in the year before the agreement and again in the year after the agreement. They data are found below:

```{r, echo = TRUE}
before <- c(12.5, -8.2, 4.1, 22.3, -5.0, 14.8, -2.3, 8.4, 3.2, 19.5,
            -11.0, 6.1, 12.9, 4.7, -3.8, 9.3, 15.0, 7.6, 1.4, 20.1,
            -6.4, 10.5, 5.2, -9.1, 13.3, 2.7, 11.8, 16.9, 3.5, 7.8)

after <- c(15.3, -6.5, 5.7, 19.9, -3.6, 15.5, -1.1, 11.2, 4.5, 20.3,
           -7.8, 7.4, 15.0, 6.3, -2.1, 9.7, 16.4, 8.5, 3.2, 21.9,
           -5.0, 12.7, 6.8, -7.0, 14.8, 4.5, 12.3, 18.1, 5.4, 8.4)
```

In the code block below, construct a 90% confidence interval for the mean difference in average trade balance where the difference is defined as after minus before. THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
t.test(after, before, paired = TRUE, conf.level = 0.9)$conf.int
```

[We are 90% confident that the true mean difference in average trade balance is between 1.1258 and 1.7342 billion dollars.]{style="color: red;"}
